pk.context: 400 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A 1990 triazole antifungal that is over 90% bioavailable and cleared mostly unchanged in urine.

clues.text: Bioavailability is over 90%, and food does not affect exposure. Protein binding is low, at 11-12%, and about 80% of the dose leaves the body unchanged in urine.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 306.27. It is a crystalline solid that is slightly soluble in water and saline.
Approved under an NDA as tablets of 50, 100, 150 and 200 mg and as a powder for oral suspension, dosed once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients, and with QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates such as erythromycin, pimozide and quinidine.
Vaginal, oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis, and prevention of candidiasis after bone marrow transplantation.
A highly selective inhibitor of fungal lanosterol 14-α-demethylase, which converts lanosterol to ergosterol. Mammalian cells are much less sensitive.
The generic name begins with F and has eleven letters.
